provenance.description: All 46 assigned Linux60 raw diagnostic differences plus independently observed byte/numeric/continuation controls; no ignore flags applied

cases.name: Declare readonly variable
cases.stdin:
declare -r var="readonly"
declare -p var

echo $var

var="change"
echo "change result: $?"
echo "var: ${var}"

declare +r var
echo "+r result: $?"
declare -p var

test_files.contents:
stable_print_assoc_array() {
    # TODO(nameref): enable use of nameref when implemented; for now
    # we assume the name of the array is assoc_array
    # local -n assoc_array=$1
    local key

    for key in $(printf "%s\n" "${!assoc_array[@]}" | sort -n); do
        echo "\"${key}\" => ${assoc_array[${key}]}"
    done
}

cases.name: Bad conversions
cases.stdin:
declare -a arr1=(a b c)
declare -A arr1
echo "Conversion result: $?"
declare -p arr1

declare -A arr2=(["x1"]=1 ["x2"]=2)
declare -a arr2
echo "Conversion result: $?"
declare -p arr2

cases.name: getopts: OPTERR non-numeric treated as enabled
cases.stdin:
OPTERR=abc
getopts "a:" myvar -x
echo "Result: $?"
echo "myvar: ${myvar}"
echo "OPTARG: ${OPTARG-UNSET}"
echo "OPTIND: ${OPTIND}"

cases.name: printf with hyphen-prefixed format string (invalid option)
cases.stdin:
printf -x
echo "Result: $?"

cases.name: printf with no arguments
cases.stdin:
printf
echo "Result: $?"

cases.name: readonly on nameref makes nameref readonly
cases.stdin:
target="value"
declare -n ref=target
readonly ref
declare -p ref
declare -p target
# Changing what ref points to should fail
declare -n ref=other 2>/dev/null
echo "exit: $?"
# But target should still be writable
target="new_value"
echo "target: $target"

cases.name: readonly target through nameref assignment
cases.stdin:
target="value"
readonly target
declare -n ref=target
ref="new_value" 2>/dev/null
echo "exit: $?"
echo "target: $target"

cases.name: test: invalid operators
cases.stdin:
test - -
echo "Result: $?"

cases.name: Unset array element with negative index out of bounds
cases.stdin:
declare -a myarray=(a b c)

echo "Initial array:"
declare -p myarray
echo

unset "myarray[-4]"
echo "After attempting to remove with index -4 (out of bounds):"
declare -p myarray
echo "Return code: $?"

cases.name: Nameref circular reference
cases.stdin:
declare -n a=b
declare -n b=a
echo "a: '${a}'"
echo "done"

cases.name: Nameref with set -u and unset target
cases.stdin:
set -u
declare -n ref=unset_target
echo "$ref"
echo "should not print"

cases.name: Nameref to empty string target name
cases.stdin:
declare -n ref=""
echo "ref: '${ref}'"
ref="value" 2>/dev/null
echo "done"

cases.name: Circular reference in assignment context
cases.stdin:
declare -n a=b
declare -n b=a
a="value" 2>/dev/null
echo "exit: $?"
echo "done"

cases.name: Nameref with readonly target - write fails
cases.stdin:
target="immutable"
declare -n ref=target
readonly ref
ref="attempt" 2>/dev/null
echo "exit: $?"
echo "target: $target"

cases.name: Nameref circular with 3 nodes
cases.stdin:
declare -n c1=c2
declare -n c2=c3
declare -n c3=c1
echo "c1: '${c1}'"
echo "exit: $?"

cases.name: Nameref to numeric-only target name
cases.stdin:
declare -n ref=123
echo "exit: $?"
echo "ref: '${ref}'"
echo "done"

cases.name: Nameref to name with special characters
cases.stdin:
declare -n ref="a-b"
echo "exit1: $?"
declare -n ref2="a.b"
echo "exit2: $?"
declare -n ref3="a+b"
echo "exit3: $?"
echo "done"

cases.name: Nameref to name with spaces
cases.stdin:
declare -n ref="a b"
echo "exit: $?"
echo "done"

cases.name: Nameref to positional parameter name
cases.stdin:
declare -n ref=1
echo "exit: $?"
echo "done"

cases.name: Nameref to @ or *
cases.stdin:
declare -n ref1="@"
echo "exit1: $?"
declare -n ref2="*"
echo "exit2: $?"
echo "done"

cases.name: Make target readonly through nameref
cases.stdin:
target="value"
declare -n ref=target
readonly ref
declare -p target
target="new" 2>/dev/null
echo "target write exit: $?"

cases.name: Circular nameref - 4 node cycle
cases.stdin:
declare -n a=b
declare -n b=c
declare -n c=d
declare -n d=a
echo "a: '${a}'"
echo "done"

cases.name: Circular nameref - write attempt
cases.stdin:
declare -n x=y
declare -n y=x
x="value" 2>/dev/null
echo "write exit: $?"
echo "done"

cases.name: Nameref to arr[@] - write attempt
cases.stdin:
arr=(a b c)
declare -n ref='arr[@]'
ref="new" 2>/dev/null
echo "exit: $?"
declare -p arr

cases.name: Circular via retarget
cases.stdin:
declare -n a=b
declare -n b=c
c="value"
echo "a: $a"
# Now make it circular
declare -n c=a
echo "a after: '${a}'"
echo "done"

cases.name: Self-reference by adding -n to existing var
cases.stdin:
x=x
declare -n x
echo "exit: $?"
declare -p x
echo "val: '${x}'"

cases.name: Array assignment through nameref-to-subscript errors
cases.stdin:
arr=(1 2 3)
declare -n ref='arr[2]'
ref=(a b c) 2>/dev/null
echo "exit: $?"
declare -p arr

cases.name: Compound array append through subscripted nameref errors
cases.stdin:
arr=(a b c)
declare -n ref='arr[0]'
ref+=(x y z) 2>/dev/null
echo "exit: $?"
echo "arr: ${arr[@]}"

cases.name: Readonly propagates through 2-level nameref chain
cases.stdin:
target="original"
declare -n middle=target
declare -n top=middle
readonly top
declare -p target
top="new" 2>/dev/null
echo "exit: $?"
middle="new" 2>/dev/null
echo "exit: $?"
target="new" 2>/dev/null
echo "exit: $?"
echo "target: $target"

cases.name: Nameref chain exceeds max depth
cases.stdin:
final_target="deep_value"
declare -n c9=final_target
declare -n c8=c9
declare -n c7=c8
declare -n c6=c7
declare -n c5=c6
declare -n c4=c5
declare -n c3=c4
declare -n c2=c3
declare -n c1=c2
echo "c1: '$c1'"
echo "done"

cases.name: Subscripted nameref with set -u when element is unset
cases.stdin:
set -u
arr=(a b c)
declare -n ref='arr[5]'
echo "$ref"
echo "should not print"

cases.name: Circular nameref with set -e does not abort script
cases.stdin:
set -e
declare -n a=b
declare -n b=a
echo "val: '${a}'"
echo "script continues"

cases.name: Nameref to unset variable with set -eu errors and exits
cases.stdin:
set -eu
declare -n ref=nonexistent
echo "$ref"
echo "should not print"

cases.name: failglob errors on unmatched glob
cases.stdin:
shopt -s failglob
echo non-existent-*.txt 2>/dev/null
echo "exit=$?"

cases.name: failglob with negation
cases.stdin:
shopt -s failglob
! echo non-existent-*.txt 2>/dev/null
echo "exit=$?"

cases.name: failglob in subshell
cases.stdin:
shopt -s failglob
(echo non-existent-*.txt; echo "inner=$?")
echo "outer=$?"

cases.name: failglob aborts compound list
cases.stdin:
shopt -s failglob
echo *.nomatch; echo "after"

cases.name: failglob in multi-member pipeline
cases.stdin:
shopt -s failglob
echo *.nomatch | cat
echo "after"

cases.name: failglob extglob pattern
cases.stdin:
shopt -s failglob
shopt -s extglob
echo @(nomatch_pattern_xyz)
echo "after"

cases.name: failglob takes precedence over nullglob
cases.stdin:
shopt -s failglob nullglob
echo non-existent-*.txt 2>/dev/null
echo "exit=$?"

cases.name: failglob on unquoted variable with glob chars
cases.stdin:
shopt -s failglob
x='*.nomatch_xyz'
echo $x 2>/dev/null
echo "exit=$?"

cases.name: Substring with a negative length reaching past the offset
cases.stdin:
var="abcdefgh"
( echo "[${var:0:-9}]" ); echo "rc=$?"
( echo "[${var:2:-7}]" ); echo "rc=$?"
( echo "[${var:8:-1}]" ); echo "rc=$?"
empty=
( echo "[${empty:0:-1}]" ); echo "rc=$?"

cases.name: Substring with negative length on arrays
Substring operator on a scalar referenced as an array
Substring with negative length on a sparse indexed array
cases.stdin:
sparse=([1]=one [5]=five [9]=nine)
( echo "[${sparse[@]:0:-1}]" ); echo "rc=$?"
( echo "[${sparse[@]:5:-1}]" ); echo "rc=$?"
( echo "[${sparse[@]:9:-1}]" ); echo "rc=$?"
( echo "[${sparse[@]:10:-1}]" ); echo "rc=$?"
( echo "[${sparse[@]:11:-1}]" ); echo "rc=$?"
unset OPTERR; getopts a opt -x; printf "status:%s\n" "$?"
OPTERR=abc; getopts a opt -x; printf "status:%s\n" "$?"
OPTERR=; getopts a opt -x; printf "status:%s\n" "$?"
OPTERR=1x; getopts a opt -x; printf "status:%s\n" "$?"
OPTERR="  -2x"; getopts a opt -x; printf "status:%s\n" "$?"
OPTERR=000; getopts a opt -x; printf "status:%s\n" "$?"
OPTERR=0x1; getopts a opt -x; printf "status:%s\n" "$?"
a=(a b c); unset 'a[-4]'; echo rc:$?; z=yes; unset 'a[-4]' z; echo multi:$? z:${z-unset}
printf -v out '%s' -x; printf '<%s>\n' "$out"; printf -- '-x\n'
printf -vone -vtwo '%s' value; printf '<%s>\n' "${one-unset}" "$two"
printf -v; echo status:$?
test $'\xff' -; echo status:$?
declare -n ref=$'\xff'; echo status:$?

shopt -s failglob; x=$'\xff*.nomatch'; echo $x
echo status:$?
